name: MCP39F521-E_MQ
title: Single-phase I2C power monitor with calculation engine and energy accumulation
summary: MCP39F521 measures a single-phase line: two 24-bit delta-sigma ADCs sample current and voltage, and a 16-bit calculation engine reports RMS current and voltage, active, reactive and apparent power, power factor and line frequency over I2C. It keeps signed import/export active and four-quadrant reactive energy in 64-bit counters, drives a zero crossing output and an event pin for sag, surge, over current and over power, and holds 512 bytes of user EEPROM. Error is 0.1 % typical over a 4000:1 range; it runs from 2.7 V to 3.6 V in a 5x5 mm 28-lead QFN.

circuits.title: Typical application: single-phase, two-wire meter
circuits.description: A 2 mΩ shunt in the line conductor L carries the load current; its two ends reach I1+ and I1- through a ferrite bead and a 1 kΩ / 33 nF low-pass on each side. The neutral passes a ferrite bead and a 499 kΩ + 499 kΩ over 1 kΩ divider (1000:1) into V1+, with 33 nF across the 1 kΩ; V1- returns to AGND through 1 kΩ with 33 nF. The shunt's minus end is the circuit's reference, DGND. A capacitive dropper (0.47 µF and 470 Ω, with a varistor and 0.01 µF across the line) feeds a zener clamp and diode into 470 µF and an MCP1754 regulator for the +3.3 V rail. DVDD and RESET sit on +3.3 V; AVDD comes through 10 Ω with 1 µF and 0.1 µF. REFIN+/OUT has 0.1 µF to AGND. SCL and SDA have 2 kΩ pull-ups and may pass an I2C isolator to the MCU. An MCP9700A on AN_IN and a 4 MHz crystal with two 22 pF capacitors are optional.

parts.note: current shunt in the line conductor L
joins the supply return DGND to AGND

notes: The shunt, the two 499 kΩ resistors and the 1 kΩ divider resistor match the default calibration registers; with 1 % parts the readings fall within about 2-3 % without calibration.
The chip's AGND, DGND and EP join on AGND; the supply return DGND reaches AGND through FB4.
NC pins 2, 3, 8, 9 and DR are left open; COMMONA and COMMONB are joined on the board.
MCLR (pin 26) has no connection given in this circuit.
The two I2C isolators are optional and have no part number; SCL and SDA end at terminals.

operation.text: Sampling is phase-locked to the line, with a whole number of samples in each line cycle. All power outputs update once per computation cycle of 2^N line cycles, N being the Accumulation Interval Parameter, so the update rate follows the line frequency.

Each channel is a PGA and a 24-bit multi-level delta-sigma modulator with a SINC3 filter, followed by a high-pass filter. The high-pass filters switch off by themselves when no AC signal is on the voltage channel. The DC Offset Current register is added right after the current ADC, and the Phase Compensation register corrects external phase error between the channels. PGA gain, ADC reset and ADC shutdown are set in System Configuration.

The PGA moves the input common mode up from AGND to an internal level inside the AGND-AVDD span, and amplifies the differential signal. The differential range is ±600 mVPEAK/GAIN with VREF = 1.2 V; the modulator's input range must not be exceeded.

Each analog input stays undistorted within ±1 V of AGND. The pin descriptions give ±6 V without damage, continuous, for the current inputs and ±2 V for the voltage inputs; the absolute maximum for all four is ±2 V.

Active and reactive power carry a sign: import (power taken by the load) is positive, export negative. The power registers hold the magnitude and SIGN_PA / SIGN_PR in System Status give the direction. Reactive power uses a 90 degree shift of the voltage channel. Four 64-bit accumulators count import and export active energy and import and export reactive energy.

When ENRG_CNTRL is 1, all four energy registers add the cycle's energy at the end of each computation cycle, at a default resolution of 1 mWh. Power under the No-Load Threshold is not counted; that register is in units of 0.01 W with a default of 100 (1.00 W). Clearing ENRG_CNTRL stops accumulation and zeroes the registers.

Two pointer registers each name an output register (Voltage RMS to Apparent Power, 0x0006 to 0x001A); after each calculation interval the chip updates the matching minimum and maximum records. Other addresses, including the 64-bit energy registers, are ignored.
The low 10 bits of the Analog Input register hold the SAR ADC result, converted once per computation cycle. With an MCP9700A on AN_IN the reading can drive the temperature compensation.

ZCD follows zero crossings of the voltage channel with under 100 µs latency: a low-pass filter takes out the fundamental and an internal circuit restores its phase delay. By default the pin toggles at each crossing, a square wave at twice the line frequency; ZCD_PULS gives a 100 µs pulse at each crossing instead, ZCD_INV inverts either form, and ZCD_OUTPUT_DIS turns the pin off.

EVENT can carry no event, any mix of voltage surge, voltage sag, over current and over power, or a level set by hand through EVENT_MANU. Over current and over power are tested once per computation cycle. Sag and surge are faster: a trailing mean square of the voltage over half a line cycle is compared with the limits at every data-ready, giving a logic-high on EVENT when mapped, in less than one line cycle; this suits detecting a power failure. Each event can latch, be cleared, and be simulated for test.

Range holds the number of right shifts (division by 2^RANGE) for current RMS, voltage RMS and power; the power byte sets active and reactive alike. Enough shift is needed to keep the output from overflowing, and little enough to keep the resolution wanted. Defaults: power 19, current 12, voltage 18.

Control code 1110, then A2 = 1 and the A1, A0 pins, so up to four devices share one bus. Each transfer is a frame between start and stop: header 0xA5, byte count, one or more command packets, checksum. Nothing in a frame runs until the stop bit, the count and the checksum are checked; a bad checksum runs none of it and returns CSFAIL 0x51. Replies begin with ACK 0x06. Data travel LSB first; a frame reads or writes at most 32 bytes in total. 100 kHz and 400 kHz are supported.
The I2C interface resets if SCL stays low longer than 2 ms; TIMEOUT_DIS turns this off. After receiving a frame the chip holds SCL low until it has processed it, for under 10 ms.
The 16-bit address pointer at 0x0000 is written only by the Set Address Pointer command; it is outside the writable register range. The command replies ACK when the address is valid.
A factory date code, YMDD, year and month in hex and day in decimal: 0xF316 is 16 February 2015.

RESET<1:0> puts one or both ADCs in soft reset: running, with output forced to 0. SHUTDOWN<1:0> turns one or both converters and their biases off, leaving leakage only; clearing it restores biases, clock and digital circuits. The RESET pin holds the whole analog front end in reset.

The internal reference corrects its first- and second-order temperature coefficients, typically 10 ppm/°C from -40 °C to +125 °C, varying from part to part. VREFCAL (default 0x42) trims the coefficient on each part; VREFEXT turns the internal reference off for an external one on REFIN+/OUT. Bypass capacitors on REFIN+/OUT improve performance but are not required.

A 4 MHz crystal with load capacitors may go on OSCI/OSCO; with no crystal or external clock found, the chip runs on its internal 4 MHz oscillator. On the internal oscillator the line frequency must be calibrated.
After each delta-sigma conversion DR pulses low, synchronous with the line so each cycle holds a whole number of samples, and the calculation engine takes an interrupt. DR is for indication only.

1. temperature (optional, with an external sensor): copy the thermistor reading into Ambient Temperature Reference Voltage; 2. line frequency (optional, on the internal oscillator): Auto-Calibrate Frequency; 3. gain at PF = 1: Auto-Calibrate Gain; 4. phase at PF ≠ 1 (optional); 5. reactive gain at PF ≠ 1 (optional): Auto-Calibrate Reactive Gain, typically at PF = 0.5. After an ACK, Save Registers To Flash keeps the result.

With stable voltage and current applied that equal Calibration Current, Calibration Voltage and Calibration Power Active, Auto-Calibrate Gain sets Gain Current RMS, Gain Voltage RMS and Gain Active Power by the gain equation. In AC mode with the high-pass filters on, offsets mostly vanish and one point suffices. Range, PGA gain and hardware must put every new gain between 25,000 and 65,535.

1 A applied reads 2300 with Gain Current RMS 33480 and Range 12; target 1000 (1 mA resolution). 33480 × 1000/2300 = 14556, below 25,000: NAK. Range 13 halves the reading to 1150 and gives 29113: ACK. Range 14 gives 58226, near the limit, a yield risk; a gain mid-range is best. For 0.1 mA resolution (target 10000), 145565 is too large; 145565/65535 = 2.2, so 2 fewer shifts: Range 10, reading 9200, gain 36391: ACK.

Needs sinusoidal voltage and current of good amplitude with a large phase shift; a displacement power factor of 0.5 is recommended. Compute Φ from the measured and expected angles and add it to the low byte of Phase Compensation; at most ±3.2 degrees can be corrected.

Done with no line voltage or current applied. AC offsets go in Offset Current RMS, Offset Active Power and Offset Reactive Power, allowing for the gain and range in each path. For DC use the high-pass filters are off and DC Offset Current removes residual DC on the current channel.

Line Frequency reads the frequency on the voltage channel, valid from 45 to 65 Hz, and reads zero in DC mode. Auto-Calibrate Frequency, with a stable voltage at the frequency held in Line Frequency Reference, sets Gain Line Frequency by the gain equation.

The sensor reading corrects the shunt's resistance drift and the internal RC oscillator's frequency drift. Three registers hold the coefficients: line frequency, current, and power (active and reactive). Their effect is small near the calibration temperature; the defaults are a starting point.
Writing 0xA5A5 to Calibration Register Delimiter, saving to flash and resetting restores the factory calibration, which stays until a new calibration is saved.

512 bytes of user EEPROM, 256 16-bit words in 32 pages of 16 bytes, readable and writable over the full supply range. Page Read returns one page of 16 bytes; Page Write takes a page number and 16 data bytes; Bulk Erase sets every word to 0xFFFF.
DVDD must start below 0.7 V and rise at 0.05 V/ms or faster; AVDD must start below 2.1 V and rise at 0.042 V/ms or faster for the internal power-on reset.
AGND goes to the analog ground plane where one exists; DGND to the digital plane, which the other digital circuits also use. The exposed pad goes to DGND.
